desk.headline: HEPS up 25% to 399c as operating profit rises 26% to R1.1bn; no interim dividend; outlook cautious on farm demand
results: Headline earnings per share rose 25% to 399c from 320c; revenue edged up 2% to R11.4bn on higher selling prices despite lower volumes.
Operating profit grew 26% to R1.1bn and the operating margin widened to 9.9% from 8%.
Mining operating profit rose 15% to R655m and Agriculture 13% to R517m; Chemicals more than doubled to R97m on lower costs and asset-sale gains.
No interim dividend was declared; R1.2bn went to shareholders through the FY26 ordinary (470c) and special (280c) dividends paid in the period, and net cash fell to R366m.

guidance.summary: Omnia gives no figures. It says Agriculture is well placed but softer crop prices, high input costs and a possible dry El Niño season could weigh on demand and margins for the rest of FY27.

points: CEO Seelan Gobalsamy credited the spread across mining, agriculture and countries for a very strong first half.
Shareholders voted 99.9% in favour of Solar Industries' proposed R21.8bn buyout at R134.50 a share; the deal still has conditions to meet.
Management said South Africa would remain a core manufacturing base under the new owner.
Omnia is still contesting SARS transfer-pricing assessments for 2014–2016 and is open to settlement or litigation.
call.source: EWN (9 Nov 2026) and Business Day (9 Nov 2026) coverage of the results

watch: Completion of the Solar Industries takeover and its remaining conditions.
Fertiliser demand in the summer planting season given crop prices and El Niño risk.
Progress on the SARS transfer-pricing dispute.
